evidence.note: Released January 21, 1933 by Mascot Pictures, so it is protected unless the notice or the 28th-year renewal failed. The renewal window is 1960-1962. The Copyright Office public-records site could not be queried by script. No renewal was found, but absence is not confirmed.

editorial:
The Whispering Shadow is a 12-chapter Mascot Pictures serial released January 21, 1933. Bela Lugosi plays Professor Adam Anton Strang, a wax-museum owner suspected of being a death-ray killer who directs his agents by television. Colbert Clark and Albert Herman directed. Karl Dane appears in what Wikipedia lists as his last role. A reuser would want it for the Lugosi casting, the early sci-fi gadgetry and the cliffhanger structure. The Internet Archive hosts all twelve chapters.

The rights trap is that the print's status is unresolved. A 1933 film is free only if its notice or its 1960-1962 renewal failed. We could not confirm either, and we checked only part of the catalog text. Search the Copyright Office records and the 1960-62 catalog volumes yourself before relying on it. An Internet Archive upload, even with a Creative Commons licence tag, does not settle the copyright. Check any feature-length cut or later release for added material.
faq: Is The Whispering Shadow (1933) safe to reuse?

Not yet confirmed. It was released in 1933, so it is free only if the notice or the 1960-62 renewal failed. Our check found no renewal but was incomplete, so verify it in the Copyright Office records and the catalog volumes before commercial use.
Does the Internet Archive's Creative Commons tag make it free to use?
No. An uploader's licence tag does not decide the film's copyright. The status depends on the original 1933 copyright and its renewal.
